point_difference_percentage_points.capture_pattern: high-burn minus unburned difference is \*\*([+-][0-9.]+) percentage points\*\*

inferential_statement_text.text: The direction of the high-burn versus unburned disagreement is repeatable, but its quantitative size is exploratory once counties rather than tracts are resampled, as recorded below.

The high-burn minus unburned difference is **+9.55 percentage points**, and its 95% percentile interval is **[+0.55, +20.89] percentage points** under the published stratified 50,000-draw tract bootstrap but **[-1.65, +16.67] percentage points** when whole counties are resampled instead of tracts; under the criterion preregistered before any result was seen, the difference is therefore **exploratory** and is not established at 95% confidence.

The two intervals answer different questions and are not interchangeable: the tract interval measures sensitivity to tract-level resampling of the binary ratio indicator at a fixed county composition, and because tracts inside one county share Overture provider mix, terrain and reference vintage it understates county-level dependence, so it is not the interval to quote when counties rather than tracts are the independent units; it also captures none of the spatial dependence, measurement error, source-vintage uncertainty, or hidden-target error.

Tracts inside one county share Overture provider mix, terrain and reference vintage, so it understates county-level dependence, and the same statistic was rechecked with a county-cluster bootstrap that was preregistered before any result was seen (`reports/discovery-postfire-county-bootstrap.json`, `scripts/audit_discovery_postfire_county_bootstrap.py`): 50,000 seeded replicates resample all 23 counties of the analysis population with replacement, every tract record of a selected county is kept, and the difference is recomputed inside each replicate.

The point estimate is unchanged, every replicate contained both focal groups (valid-replicate fraction 1.0), and 95.99% of valid replicates point the same way, but the 95% percentile interval widens from [+0.55, +20.89] to [-1.65, +16.67] percentage points, so its lower bound is no longer above zero.

Under the preregistered criterion the quantitative difference is therefore **exploratory**: the direction is repeatable in almost every county resample, while this sample does not support it at 95% confidence once counties, rather than tracts, are treated as the independent units.

classification_rules.note: an inferential statement about the difference is a sentence that both talks about the difference and uses an inferential, confidence or robustness cue; it is qualified when the same sentence names the clustered result. Exemptions are definitional or descriptive sentences about the ratio, the table or the exclusions, never inference about the difference.

hidden_target_patterns: labels these tracts as coverage gaps
language.note: forbidden and hidden-target patterns are searched only in affirmative prose: a sentence carrying a negation marker is a disclosure, not a claim

contrast_phrases: rather than tracts are the independent units
contrast_requirement.note: one sentence must put the two designs in the same breath, so a reader cannot take tract-resampling sensitivity for clustered inference

qualification.near_finding_scope: finding block (Status line through the end of the post-fire Reproducibility section)

preregistration.intent: Documentation screen. Count the inferential statements about the high-burn versus unburned difference that are not qualified by the preregistered county-cluster result, in the two organiser-facing writeups, and require exact agreement with the frozen reports. This screen does not promote an estimator, does not re-run any resampling, and does not change any preregistered design.
preregistration.title: County-cluster uncertainty must be visible wherever the high-burn versus unburned difference is claimed
